en: One concept that aims to
help with hallucinations or solve the
problem of hallucinations beside simply
making better models
is the concept of grounding,
which means that the software in which a
large language model runs, let's say
ChatGPT, for example, tries to
ground the answers a model makes in clear
sources, in websites or in references to
statements or paragraphs in text documents
that you maybe provided to the model. So for
example, if you're asking ChatGPT to
summarize a PDF document, the output may
reference certain pages where a statement
was made when creating that summary. And
that process is called grounding. It means
that the software in which the large
language model runs behind the scenes nudges
the model to not just output its answer
or its result for which you asked it, but
that it also must clearly point at the
sources, at the concrete statements on which
an answer may be based.
And therefore, another part of grounding, of
course, is that you want to provide your
model, your large language model, with any
sources that are relevant for producing a
better answer.
That may be something you do explicitly by,
for example, attaching the PDF documents
which you want the model to summarize or use
as sources,
or by providing certain links to websites
you want the model to analyze.
Or it may also happen indirectly by the
tool,
again ChatGPT or maybe Claude, which runs
the model, which may include search so that
it automatically searches the web to produce
better results. And that is of course
something which modern AI tools like ChatGPT
or Claude typically do automatically. But
All these things combined then make up this
concept of grounding.
